requirement:
TBV automatically redacts recognized credentials in source excerpts delivered
by its inspection tools and in node text supplied to its agent requests.
The built-in rules replace recognized secret regions with redaction markers
while preserving line breaks. SDK-supplied outline languages use the same redacted
regions, so changing only a recognized credential does not change its
structural fingerprint.

Loaded source snapshots retain the original text for selection and spans;
redaction applies when preparing model-visible text and structural hashes.
Filesystem evidence storage preserves the supplied record. Applications supply
their own answer values and remain responsible for what those answers contain.
Habeas additionally recognizes explicit credentials in its configuration files
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.credentials`.
rationale:
I found no test-adequacy gap for `requirements.sdk.sources.redaction`. The obligations and the tests that cover them are below.

**Redaction of delivered source excerpts and node text.** This is covered at each delivery path.
- `read_source` is covered by `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[fixed_source_reads_redact_delivery_and_propagate_preparation_errors]`. It asserts that the token is absent from the returned text, that `[REDACTED:GitHub Token]` is present, and that the line count is preserved. It also asserts that the dependency fingerprint is taken from the raw content.
- `read_node` and the queued `contents_of_current_node` request are covered by `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[queued_contents_and_graph_read_tools_redact_credentials_before_delivery]`. It checks every request's chat history for the marker and for the absence of the raw secret. The test text shows a literal marker in place of the secret. That is the review tool's own redaction of the source I was given, so I did not treat the apparent contradiction as a defect. The test also checks that the dependency fingerprint and the stored graph contents keep the raw original.
- Paged reads are covered by `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/validation.rs#fn[direct_paged_empty_failed_and_redacted_reads_keep_delivery_accounting]`. It reassembles the paged output, checks the token is gone, the marker is present and the line count is unchanged. It also checks that the dependency fingerprint is the raw one.
- The other tools in `ProjectSources` dispatch, such as `search_text`, share one final `redact_text` call on the serialized output. The `read_source` test exercises that call, and the requirement draws no distinctions between tools, so I did not require a separate test for each.

**Built-in rules replace recognized regions with markers and preserve line breaks.** These tests are in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/redaction/tests.rs`.
- `private_keys_are_redacted_from_header_through_body_keeping_lines` covers multi-line private keys, including inside Rust source, with line-count preservation.
- `tokens_in_code_are_redacted_without_adjacent_code` checks that the surrounding code is untouched.
- `regions_extend_both_ways_keep_crlf_and_scan_past_a_mebibyte` covers CRLF preservation, adjacent-region merging, newline counts, and inputs larger than a mebibyte.
- `slices_concatenate_to_the_redacted_whole` covers slice and whole-text consistency.
- `heuristic_findings_alone_are_not_redacted` checks that only recognized credentials are redacted.
- `configuration_keys_do_not_add_sdk_specific_secret_rules` checks that the SDK adds no configuration-key rules. The Habeas-specific additions fall under the cited `requirements.authoring.credentials`, which is context only.

**Outline languages share the redacted regions, so a credential-only change leaves the fingerprint unchanged.**
- `src/redaction/configuration_tests.rs#fn[hashes_do_not_depend_on_credential_values]` asserts equal hashes for Rust and text when only the token differs. It asserts different hashes when code outside the region changes. It also covers `habeas.toml` against a generic `.toml`.
- `src/redaction/configuration_tests.rs#fn[redaction_never_changes_an_outline]` checks the outline structure for YAML, Rust, TOML, Markdown and text.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[formatted_contents_redact_credentials_while_retaining_raw_text_and_spans]` checks that the fingerprint is equal for two different tokens.

**Snapshots retain original text for selection and spans.** The same `outline_content.rs` test asserts that `contents.text()` equals the raw source. It also asserts that the selected node's `text()` still contains the token while its `format()` does not.

**Filesystem evidence storage preserves the supplied record, and application answers are not redacted.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/storage.rs#fn[storage_preserves_completed_answers_containing_credential_shaped_text]` stores an answer containing a token-shaped string. It asserts an exact round trip and that the token appears in the file on disk.

No obligation is untested, and the assertions enforce the required outcomes, so the tests are adequate.

text: :::{req} redaction
TBV automatically redacts recognized credentials in source excerpts delivered
by its inspection tools and in node text supplied to its agent requests.
The built-in rules replace recognized secret regions with redaction markers
while preserving line breaks. SDK-supplied outline languages use the same redacted
regions, so changing only a recognized credential does not change its
structural fingerprint.
Loaded source snapshots retain the original text for selection and spans;
redaction applies when preparing model-visible text and structural hashes.
Filesystem evidence storage preserves the supplied record. Applications supply
their own answer values and remain responsible for what those answers contain.
Habeas additionally recognizes explicit credentials in its configuration files
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.credentials`.
:::{req} credentials
Bedrock configurations MAY supply `credentials` containing nonempty
`access_key_id`, `secret_access_key`, and optional nonempty `session_token`.
Ollama and OpenAI configurations MAY supply a nonempty `api_key`. Habeas MUST reject a
Bedrock record combining explicit credentials with `aws_profile`, and an Ollama or OpenAI
record combining `api_key` with `api_key_env`.
Explicit credentials MUST be passed directly to the selected provider without
changing process environment variables or writing credential files. Saved
explicit values MUST round-trip; credentials resolved from profiles or the
environment MUST NOT be serialized back. Debug output, configuration diagnostics,
usage records, and initial prompts MUST NOT include credential values. TOML
diagnostics MUST NOT echo credential-containing source lines. A configuration
file containing explicit credentials MAY be read as source; its credential
values MUST be redacted under {cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`.
Validation MUST report a workspace `habeas.toml` present in the Git index that
contains explicit credentials, naming the file and the credential fields and
recommending credential-source references, because committed credentials leak.
Documentation MUST discourage literal credentials in workspace files and
recommend AWS profiles or environment-variable references. Examples MUST use
placeholders and explain that workspace files may be committed or read as source
when explicitly allowed.
